main.summary: Yan Zhenqing mourns his nephew Jiming, killed in the An Lushan rebellion. He praises the boy's early promise, recalls how the two brothers rose against the rebels at Changshan and Pingyuan, the opening of the Tumen pass, and the fall of the city that cost father and son their lives, and ends with how he brought back the head and coffin.
main.translation:
In the first year of the Qianyuan era, the year wuxu, on the third day of the ninth month, renshen: I, Zhenqing, thirteenth uncle, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, Governor of Puzhou with the imperial tally, Commander of Puzhou, Senior Commandant of Light Chariots, Marquis of Danyang, offer clear wine and assorted dishes in sacrifice to the spirit of my departed nephew Jiming, posthumously Grand Master of Remonstrance for the Heir Apparent, and say:
You were born upright and outstanding, and from early youth showed fine virtue. In the ancestral temple you would have been a precious vessel; in the courtyard, an orchid and a jade tree. Always you gladdened our hearts, and we hoped to see you enjoy good fortune and emolument.
Who could have imagined that rebels would seize their moment, take up arms and defy the throne? Your father gave all his loyalty and held Changshan as governor. I, at that time, had my own orders and was at Pingyuan. My kind elder brother cared for me and sent you to bring me his word. After you had gone back, the Tumen pass was opened. Once Tumen was open, the rebels' fierce power was greatly checked. But the traitor ministers did not come to the rescue, and the lone city was besieged and pressed hard. The father fell and the son died; the nest was overturned and the eggs were smashed. Heaven did not repent of the calamity, and who was to suffer such cruelty? When I think of the harm you met, even a hundred lives could not redeem you. Alas, the grief!
I received Heaven's favour and was moved to govern the region of Heguan, on the river frontier. Quanming recently went again to Changshan, which had fallen once more, and carried your head and your coffin, and came back together with them. When I touch these memories my heart breaks; grief shakes my spirit and my face. When the day comes, in the distant time, I will divine a resting place for you. If your soul has knowledge, do not sigh that you have long been a guest far from home. Alas, the grief! Accept this offering!

keyLines.en: You were born upright and outstanding, and from early youth showed fine virtue.
keyLines.note: Praises Jiming as naturally upright and marked out by virtue from a young age.

keyLines.en: In the ancestral temple you would have been a precious vessel; in the courtyard, an orchid and a jade tree.
keyLines.note: Two images, the temple vessel and the orchid and jade tree, show that he was a pillar of the family and a fine young man.

keyLines.en: The father fell and the son died; the nest was overturned and the eggs were smashed.
keyLines.note: Changshan fell and Yan Gaoqing and his son Jiming were killed together; the overturned nest and smashed eggs stand for the destruction of a whole family.

keyLines.en: Heaven did not repent of the calamity, and who was to suffer such cruelty?
keyLines.note: An accusation against Heaven for showing no pity and letting the disaster run so deep; his anger and grief are not eased.

keyLines.en: When I think of the harm you met, even a hundred lives could not redeem you.
keyLines.note: Even a hundred lives given in exchange could not buy him back; it is boundless grief.

keyLines.en: If your soul has knowledge, do not sigh that you have long been a guest far from home.
keyLines.note: The closing words comfort the dead: if you can still know anything, do not lament dying in a strange land.

glossary.en: Qianyuan yuannian - first year of Qianyuan
glossary.note: A reign-period of Emperor Suzong of the Tang dynasty (618-907); this is 758, the year wuxu in the sixty-year cycle.
Yan Zhenqing was thirteenth among the cousins of his generation, and speaks of himself in that family order.
A costly ritual vessel for holding millet in the ancestral temple; a figure for a gifted person.
From 'orchid and jade tree', a way of praising a fine young man in the family.

glossary.en: jian gu - good fortune and emolument
glossary.note: Jian means good fortune and gu means official pay, so together they mean blessings and rank.
Yan Gaoqing, Jiming's father, was governor of Changshan, and Yan Zhenqing governor of Pingyuan. Each raised troops against the rebels at the start of the An Lushan rebellion.
Another name for the Jingxing pass, a key route in Hebei; once it was opened, the rebels' rear could be cut.

glossary.en: zanshan daifu - Grand Master of Remonstrance
glossary.note: An official of the Heir Apparent's household, given to Jiming after his death as an honour.

main.background: This scroll, also known as the Draft for a Nephew, is the draft of a funeral address that Yan Zhenqing wrote in 758 for his nephew Yan Jiming, who died in the An Lushan rebellion. The original ink on paper is in the National Palace Museum, Taipei. It is written throughout in running-cursive script: it begins with composure, and as grief and anger mount the brush becomes wilder, while the crossings-out show real feeling. It is called the second-best running script in the world, after the Orchid Pavilion Preface. It is the summit of Tang running-cursive script, and the best model for learning Yan's running script and seeing how calligraphy and emotion join.
